issue_context.title: OpenGL: TextureArrays and Texture3D samplers not implemented yet
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

Godot Engine v4.0.beta10

### System information

archlinux; vulkan on dedicated `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU`; opengl3 on integrated `AMD Radeon Graphics (renoir, LLVM 14.0.6, DRM 3.49, 6.1.1-arch1-1)`

### Issue description

With the opengl3 backend a shader will read a Samper2dArray uniform as being completely black.

opengl3:
![texturearray_opengl3](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7968950/211161142-48379a1b-ea3c-4529-bbda-ad837f56bbfb.png)

vulkan:
![texturearray_vulkan](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7968950/211161147-d84389cb-737f-4229-9984-36d9dd12a0ce.png)

used shader:
```
shader_type spatial;

uniform sampler2DArray textures : source_color, filter_linear_mipmap;

void fragment() {
	ALBEDO = texture(textures, vec3(UV, 1.0)).xyz;
}
```

### Steps to reproduce

Create a scene with a meshinstance3d with the shader above as a material.
Give that shader a Texture2DArray as parameter.
With the vulkan renderer this will run fine, but with opengl3 the texture is read as being completely black.

### Minimal reproduction project

[sampler2darray.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/10366728/sampler2darray.zip)
comments: Looks like this hasn't been implemented yet in the gl_compatibility nor have 3D textures. It should not be a lot of work to implement.

Good news: as of Godot 4.1 RC1, TextureArrays are now functional in the OpenGL Compatibility renderer. 👍  Texture3Ds are still not implemented yet.

The cube should be a bright color, not black:

![Image3](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/72348938/486c5fd7-2716-4ebd-a1e5-52c56c455e96)

review_comments:
I would prefer to keep the implementation closer to the RD renderer and cache the texture. That way we can avoid expensive GPU readback as much as possible

https://github.com/clayjohn/godot/blob/1b80f21abff039dbf3e319698d118712c3e4f77f/servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/texture_storage.cpp#L1332

The RD renderer caches the slice info for the texture and the raw data so that the images can be reconstructed when needed. This approach makes sense for Texture3D since it is never used as a framebuffer. So caching the data is fine (it just needs to e updated when calling ``texture_3d_update()``)

Since OpenGL doesn't have direct buffer access caching slices doesn't really seem to make sense, but I think that my approach with caching `Ref<Image>` objects that are being uploaded to the GPU should work well?
I agree. I think caching makes sense here.
